headline: Bruins Agree To Three-Year Extension With Forward Marat Khusnutdinov
take:
The Hockey News and The Athletic report that the Bruins have signed forward Marat Khusnutdinov to a three-year extension, worth $3.95 million per The Athletic. The 24-year-old scored 15 goals and 33 points last season and is in the second year of a two-year, $1.85 million deal.

So far this season, the numbers back up the bet. Khusnutdinov has two goals and five points in 10 games, and his goals are close to what his chances say he should have (1.69 expected goals, which measures the quality of his shots, against two actual). That means he isn't running hot. The Bruins also control play with him on the ice: they hold about 55 percent of the expected goals at 5-on-5 in his minutes, and their share of the chances rises by about 3.4 percentage points when he plays. He gets only 13.7 minutes a game, so the production comes in a depth role. The team context matters too. Boston is 7-2-1, but its overall share of expected goals is 48.8 percent, and the results lean on goaltending (9.3 goals saved above expected). A steady, chance-driving forward at that price helps a team that has been getting by on its goalies.
